checks.command: bash scripts/with-node.sh node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='document deadline closes|host prompt deadline does not wait|HTTP 200 followed|cancellation after|Pi timeout|concurrent jobs' tests/extraction/runtime.test.ts

initial_document_check.note: Initial proof before adding the related regressions and delayed-SDK-settlement wrapper test; not an additional distinct test.

new_and_related_runtime_coverage: A 600ms document deadline ends a run while the physical request still has its configured 120000ms deadline.
The latest observed run returned in 609ms; its stalled response was closed by the client 561ms after receipt, before fixture cleanup and without the server fail-safe.
One committed candidate and one explicitly completed block survive; two missing blocks remain explicit, and reopen restores the partial run and candidate.
No retry, summary or reconciling stage starts; no later model request or business event appears during a 350ms observation after stopping.
The interrupted HTTP 200 request retains nonzero conservative input/output reservation and an explicit missing-usage status.
A delayed SDK-prompt-settlement test wrapper is still pending when the host returns at 501ms for a 500ms deadline; the physical SSE response has already been closed.
The separate 80ms per-request stalled-SSE deadline, external cancellation and existing Pi timeout regressions still pass.
Two concurrent jobs sharing the same in-process budget instance cannot both reserve the final input allowance; only one reaches loopback and the other is denied before physical I/O.
A requested document deadline above the authorized 900000ms maximum is rejected before model network activity.

prior_line_index_regression.source_snapshot_note: Original hashes/logs and hash-verified owned test/fixture snapshots are preserved; no historical implementation source was reconstructed.

historical_implementation_failures.case: External cancellation incorrectly emitted a retry event
Unavailable catalog did not preflight an invalid selected cancer
Repeated human-protected automatic update created another proposal

limitations: Only these six affected tests and TypeScript checks were run after the hard document-stop change; all 36 runtime cases and the older full suites were not repeated.
The initial one-test proof is included in the six-test total; the separate historical 8, 29 and 144-test results belong to their archived source versions.
The delayed SDK-settlement wrapper deliberately simulates delayed promise completion; this agent did not reproduce the real gateway 921-second run or call a paid model.
The 600ms document and 500ms prompt deadlines exercise supported shorter limits and do not measure real 900-second document latency.
The concurrent-budget test covers one shared budget instance in one process; it does not establish cross-process or independent-ledger locking.
The post-stop quiet observation is bounded to 350ms; no indefinite background-liveness guarantee is inferred.
These are engineering tests, not medical correctness, recall, gold-annotation or billing validation.
